cls: Skeletal muscle relaxant (central GABA-B receptor agonist)
pharm: Stimulates GABA-B receptors in the spinal cord, inhibiting mono- and polysynaptic reflexes to reduce skeletal muscle spasticity.
quick: 5 mg three times daily, titrate to 40-80 mg/day
May take with or without food
Use only if benefit outweighs risk
Excreted in milk; use with caution
Reduce dose; accumulates in renal impairment
summary: Baclofen is a centrally acting GABA-B agonist used to relieve the signs and symptoms of spasticity from multiple sclerosis (especially flexor spasms, pain, clonus, and muscular rigidity) and may help spinal cord injury or disease. It is titrated slowly to a usual range of 40-80 mg/day (max 80 mg/day orally). Common effects are drowsiness, dizziness, and weakness. Abrupt withdrawal can cause hallucinations, seizures, high fever, rebound spasticity, and rhabdomyolysis, so it must be tapered.
indications: Alleviation of signs and symptoms of spasticity resulting from multiple sclerosis (flexor spasms, pain, clonus, muscular rigidity)
May be of value in patients with spinal cord injuries and other spinal cord diseases

dosage.d: 5 mg three times daily x3 days, then 10 mg TID x3 days, then 15 mg TID x3 days, then 20 mg TID x3 days

dosage.n: Do not exceed 80 mg/day (20 mg four times daily)

dosage.d: Withdraw slowly if no benefit after a reasonable trial
Reduce dose (baclofen is renally excreted and accumulates)

admin: Start low and titrate gradually to the lowest effective dose
May be taken with or without food; take with food if GI upset occurs
Do not stop abruptly; taper to avoid serious withdrawal
Reduce dose in renal impairment and in the elderly
moa: Baclofen is a structural analog of the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA. It acts primarily at the spinal cord level as an agonist at GABA-B receptors, inhibiting the release of excitatory neurotransmitters and reducing the transmission of mono- and polysynaptic reflexes. This decreases the frequency and severity of muscle spasms and relieves the rigidity and clonus associated with spasticity. It may also have central depressant effects.

relative: Patients who use spasticity to maintain posture/balance or for function
monitor: Withdrawal symptoms on any dose change/discontinuation

preg: There are no adequate studies in pregnant women; baclofen crosses the placenta. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Neonatal withdrawal has been reported with maternal use.
lact: Baclofen is excreted in human milk; use with caution in breastfeeding mothers and monitor the infant for sedation and poor feeding.
renal: Baclofen is excreted largely unchanged by the kidneys and accumulates in renal impairment, increasing the risk of toxicity (sedation, confusion, respiratory depression). Reduce the dose and monitor closely; consider lower doses in dialysis patients.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is established for hepatic impairment; monitor clinically.

major: CNS depressants (opioids, benzodiazepines, sedatives) - additive sedation and respiratory depression
moderate: Tricyclic antidepressants (may potentiate effect, marked muscle hypotonia)
minor: Levodopa/carbidopa (reports of worsened mental confusion, agitation)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it markedly increases sedation and CNS depression.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause increases in AST, alkaline phosphatase, and blood glucose.

serious: Severe CNS/respiratory depression (especially overdose or renal failure)

monitoring: Signs of withdrawal during dose changes
counsel: Do not stop this medicine suddenly; stopping abruptly can cause hallucinations, seizures, or serious illness
It may make you drowsy or dizzy - avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you
Avoid alcohol and other sedating medicines
Take the lowest dose that controls your symptoms
Report worsening weakness, confusion, mood changes, or difficulty passing urine
pk: Hours to days; titration over weeks for full effect
Dosed three to four times daily
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light and moisture
pearls: Never discontinue abruptly - taper to avoid withdrawal seizures, hyperthermia, and rhabdomyolysis
Renally cleared; reduce dose and monitor closely in renal impairment and the elderly
Overdose causes profound CNS and respiratory depression that can mimic brain death
Avoid reducing tone that a patient relies on for posture, balance, or transfers
Additive sedation with opioids, benzodiazepines, and alcohol
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and continue your regular schedule. Do not double the dose, and never skip doses repeatedly, which risks withdrawal.
overdose: Overdose produces marked CNS depression, drowsiness progressing to coma, respiratory depression, hypotonia, hypo- or hypertension, and seizures. Management is supportive: secure the airway and support ventilation, give activated charcoal early if appropriate, maintain blood pressure, and treat seizures. There is no specific antidote; baclofen is removed by hemodialysis in significant renal impairment.
